About This Job
Care Assistant (Care Professional)
Home Instead East Nottingham
Join Our Award-Winning Team
Make a real difference in your community. We’re looking for kind, reliable people to support clients in their own homes across East Nottingham and surrounding areas.
Whether you’re experienced or new to care, we provide industry-leading training and ongoing support to help you succeed and thrive.
Areas Covered
Melton Mowbray & surrounding villages, Bingham & Radcliffe-on-Trent, Newark & Collingham, Southwell & Trent Valley villages, and parts of Nottingham (Clifton & Gedling).

Additional Information
Pay & Hours
• £13.50 per hour (weekdays)
• £16.50 per hour (weekends)
• Double pay on Bank Holidays
• Paid travel time between visits (£12.85 per hour)
Shift patterns:
• We offer very flexible scheduling rather than fixed set shifts. However, the following requirements apply:
• All Care Professionals must work a minimum of two days per week that include anti-social hours, meaning starting at 6:45am or finishing at 10:00pm.
We do not operate on strict shift blocks (e.g. 7am–3pm or 3pm–10pm). Instead, we build schedules around each Care Professional’s availability while ensuring service needs are met and the above requirements are fulfilled.
• Care Professionals must work alternate weekends.
• We have very flexible weekly working hours, but candidates must provide a minimum availability of 10 hours per week, while still meeting our required conditions (minimum two days including anti-social hours and alternate weekends).
• The role initially operates on a 0-hour contract during the probationary period. After successfully completing probation, we are able to offer an average-hours contract based on the hours you have consistently worked.
Why Join Home Instead?
• 2025 Award-Winning Training & Development
• No experience needed – full training provided
• Ongoing learning and career development
• Supportive Buddy Scheme when you start
• Employee Assistance Programme (wellbeing support)
• Paid annual leave & pension scheme
• DBS cost reimbursed after probation
• Paid MOT after 1 year of service
• Recognition & reward programmes
We also prioritise quality care:
• Minimum 1-hour morning visits
• Minimum 45-minute afternoon visits
• Time to build meaningful relationships and no rushed care
Your Role
As a Care Assistant, you’ll help clients live independently in their own homes by:
• Supporting them to stay safe, comfortable, and secure
• Providing personal care with dignity and respect
• Preparing meals and assisting with daily routines
• Offering companionship and emotional support
• Assisting with medication reminders
• Encouraging independence and promoting wellbeing
This is a role where you can make a genuine difference every single day.
What You’ll Need
• A caring, patient, and reliable nature
• Full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle
• Availability to work alternate weekends
• No formal qualifications required, full training provided
Apply Now
Start a rewarding career where you’re valued, supported, and truly make an impact.
Apply today and we’ll arrange a friendly, confidential chat at a time that suits you.
Job Types: Full-time, Part-time, Zero hours contract

About This Job
Building Inspector
Are you interested in being a Building Inspector? This could be your opportunity to excel as a Building Inspector within one of our Building Control teams, playing a critical role in safeguarding public safety, supporting sustainable building practices, and maintaining high standards in the built environment whilst supporting SOCOTEC’s continued success.
As SOCOTEC grows, so do our teams. We’re looking for a dedicated Building Inspector to join our Building & Real Estate division and wear the SOCOTEC badge with pride.
We are seeking a proactive, reliable, and flexible Building Inspector to join the Building Control team. In this role, you will be inspecting construction sites at various stages, advising on regulatory requirements, and working collaboratively with architects, builders and developers to ensure safe, structurally sound, and code-compliant buildings.
The tasks you will undertake will include (but are not limited to):
• Conduct comprehensive site inspections and regulatory assessments – Perform building inspections at various construction stages to ensure compliance with Building Regulations, review structural, architectural, and mechanical designs, assess building materials, construction specifications, and fire strategies against relevant Building Regulations and allied legislation
• Supervise inspection activities and enforce regulatory compliance – Act as a Registered Building Inspector within your competency and registered class, supervise lower-class RBIs and graduate trainees, interpret and enforce national and local building regulations (including fire safety, energy efficiency, accessibility, and environmental requirements), and issue formal notices on compliance breaches under the Building Safety Act 2022
• Prepare detailed compliance documentation and provide consultancy services – Produce comprehensive inspection reports, compliance certificates, and regulatory approval documentation, maintain accurate records ensuring traceability and compliance with local authority requirements, and assist clients with Building Regulations consultancy advice where SOCOTEC is not acting as the Registered Building Control Approver

Qualifications
To be a successful  Building Inspector, you should be able to demonstrate:
• Professional qualification and regulatory registration at senior level – Hold membership of RICS, CABE or equivalent (or be qualified by suitable experience), ensure CPD requirements are met to broaden and develop skills, and demonstrate compliance through registration as an RBI at an appropriate level (3G/3H)
• Excellent communication and client relationship management skills – Demonstrate strong interpersonal and relationship-building abilities to work effectively with clients and deliver excellent client care across all interactions and project engagements
• Self-starting problem-solver with technical expertise – Show ability to work independently as well as part of large project teams, analyse complex issues, develop suitable solutions, implement these solutions effectively, and keep up to date with changes in building codes, regulations, and industry best practices

Additional Information
Why SOCOTEC?
Join a thriving community of over 2,000 industry professionals who are passionate about making a real difference. At SOCOTEC UK, we're not just delivering services - we're shaping the future of testing, inspection, and certification across the nation.
What sets us apart? Our people. We've built our reputation on attracting exceptional talent like you and empowering them to deliver excellence at every turn. Our comprehensive range of TIC services means you'll have the opportunity to work on diverse, challenging projects that truly matter.
In this role, you won't just be another employee - you'll be a key player in our continued success story. Your expertise will directly contribute to our mission of building a safer, more sustainable world, while you grow your career alongside some of the industry's finest professionals.
Your Career, Your Way
Build a traditional career path or explore opportunities across multiple disciplines - all within SOCOTEC. Your choice, your direction.
Work Your Way
Local, national, or global projects. Office-based, remote, or hybrid. We offer the flexibility that empowers you to perform at your best.
Committed to Your Growth
From day one, you'll have access to comprehensive training, mentorship, and development programs. We support every step of your professional journey. #YouGrowWeGrow
Think you've got what it takes to add value to our success? We would love to hear from you and look forward to receiving your application.
Building a safer and more sustainable world is the core mission we set out to achieve at SOCOTEC, it is at the heart of everything that we do. We are committed to acting as a key player in society, investing in innovative solutions to ensure social and environmental concerns are at the forefront of all of our business operations.

About This Job
Railway engineering is one of the most important ways that AECOM delivers a better world – we work on huge, complex and challenging railway infrastructure projects that increase urban and inter-city mobility for millions of people. AECOM is a global innovator in high-speed and urban transportation. Recent projects include major track improvements for the Southern Renewals Enterprise in England’s busiest passenger corridors, the Hong Kong–Shenzhen Western Rail Link (Hung Shui Kiu–Qianhai), the Elephant & Castle Station capacity upgrade in London, and key design and asset protection services for Network Rail frameworks across the UK, as well as delivering components of High Speed 2 and supporting global initiatives in sustainable rail.
We are looking for graduates who are team players and open thinkers who want to contribute to some of the biggest challenges in transportation infrastructure.
Job Responsibilities
Selected candidates will be enrolled on our Graduate Development Programme and have the opportunity to develop their skills within a supportive environment that encourages curiosity, collaboration and innovation. As part of the Rail Mechanical Engineering team, you will contribute to the design, development and delivery of mechanical systems that support the safe, efficient and sustainable operation of the railway network.
You will gain experience across a range of rail projects, working closely with experienced engineers and multidisciplinary teams to deliver high-quality engineering solutions. Typical responsibilities include:
• Assisting in the design of mechanical systems for railway stations, depots, tunnels and other rail infrastructure.
• Undertaking engineering calculations, technical assessments and design studies in accordance with industry standards and client requirements.
• Supporting site surveys, inspections and condition assessments to inform design development and asset management strategies.
• Using industry-leading software and BIM tools to produce drawings, models, specifications and design documentation.
• Collaborating with colleagues across civil, electrical, structural, signalling and telecoms disciplines to deliver integrated engineering solutions.
• Supporting the planning and coordination of construction and commissioning activities.
• Ensuring designs promote sustainability, energy efficiency, maintainability and whole-life asset performance.
• Participating in project reviews, technical workshops and client meetings to develop communication and project delivery skills.
• Contributing to innovative engineering solutions that improve safety, reliability and passenger experience across the rail network.
Throughout the programme, you will have the opportunity to develop both your technical and professional skills, gaining experience that supports your journey towards chartership and a rewarding career within the rail industry.

Qualifications
• BEng in Mechanical Engineering with a 2:1 classification (or equivalent) or above.
• MEng in Mechanical Engineering would be advantageous.
• Modules in Rail Engineering, Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics, HVAC, Building Services, Power Systems or related disciplines would be advantageous.
• Demonstrable interest in Rail and Mechanical Engineering and developing a career within the industry.
• Ability to demonstrate a good technical understanding of mechanical engineering principles and their application within transportation infrastructure.
• Willing and able to work towards chartership with the Institution of Mechanical Engineers (IMechE).
• Good Microsoft Office skills, including Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
• Strong communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with clients, colleagues, stakeholders and contractors.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Enthusiastic, motivated and driven to learn and develop.
• Ability to prioritise and manage workloads effectively while working collaboratively within a team environment.
• Ability to work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team while maintaining initiative and focus.

Additional Information
• Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since CVs will be reviewed, and candidates selected on a rolling recruitment basis for either immediate or advanced offer start.
• You may include a covering letter with your application. If available, please provide your predicted and/or obtained academic grades, as well as details of the dates you are able to work and the locations you are interested in.
• You must have the right to work in the UK.
At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. You will help us foster a safe and respectful workplace, where we invite everyone to bring their whole selves to work using their unique talents, backgrounds and expertise to create transformational outcomes for our clients.

About This Job
The Recurring Payin team owns the Direct Debit API that powers automated payments into Wise. Underneath this, we are building a platform that allows customers to easily schedule top-ups or business collections.
The platform is also built on top of our internal Payin Platform rails; which is a critical component to the Wise money-movement machine and we’re looking for an engineer motivated to come and help us build for this.
We primarily offer APIs for any partner looking to set up automated funding or pre-authorizations. From setting up GBP balance top ups automatically to allowing business partners collect EUR bills monthly without having the customer go through the flow every time; our platform aims to consolidate all these use-cases.
We aim to allow customers to give a one time permission (pre-authorization) for Wise to pull money across any payment method, a USD bank account or a EUR issued bank card; you name it.
Job Responsibilities:
•
Design, develop, test, and maintain backend services written in Java and Kotlin using the Spring Boot framework, deployed on cloud infrastructure (AWS)
•
Build and maintain RESTful APIs that serve millions of customers across web and mobile platforms
•
Develop and optimise services powering the card pay-in payment method — one of the most popular payment methods, enabling Wise customers to move around £1 billion every month
•
Design and implement database schemas, write and optimise SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases handling high-volume transactional data
•
Build and maintain event-driven architectures using Apache Kafka for asynchronous processing of financial events across distributed services
•
Develop and maintain a payment orchestration system that dynamically routes payments across Payment Service Providers to optimize for cost and reliability
•
Write automated tests (unit, integration, and end-to-end) to ensure correctness and reliability of financial systems
•
Conduct code reviews for team members, ensuring code quality, security, and adherence to engineering standards
•
Participate in on-call rotations to monitor and respond to production incidents for Tier 2 critical services
•
Collaborate with product managers, designers, analysts, and engineers across other teams to deliver cross-functional projects
•
Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, scalability issues, and technical debt in existing systems
•
Ensure development follows security best practices, particularly around handling of sensitive financial data and compliance with financial regulations

About the Role
The UK water sector is entering a period of unprecedented investment and transformation. As Egis accelerates the growth of its Water Business in the UK, we are building a high-performing Process Engineering team to help shape this next chapter.
We are inviting applicants who want to play a meaningful role in delivering major water and wastewater programmes in the UK municipal and industrial sectors. Key Responsibilities
• Lead process design delivery on multidisciplinary water/wastewater treatment projects across the full design lifecycle.
• Act as process technical lead on projects, owning design strategy, treatment process selection, key decisions, interfaces, risks and quality of deliverables.
• Review and approve process calculations, mass balances, PFDs, P&IDs, basis of design reports, specifications, technical notes, models and supplier/contractor submissions.
• Lead process modelling and simulation activities using tools such as BioWin, SUMO, Dynamizu or equivalent packages.
• Lead optioneering, process capacity assessments, value engineering, design reviews, HAZOP/SWIFT, commissioning strategy and performance testing input.
• Drive multidisciplinary coordination across Mechanical, EICA, civil/structural, architectural, MEP, construction, commissioning and operations teams.
• Promote lean and digitally enabled delivery through standardised tools, process models, automation, data analysis and reusable templates.
• Provide technical assurance and support project managers with technical risk, scope, resourcing, programme and change control.
• Mentor and manage engineers where appropriate, supporting recruitment, development and chartership progression.
• Contribute to bids, client engagement, opportunity shaping and growth of the process capability.

Qualifications
Minimum Requirements
• BEng/MEng or equivalent in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering or closely related discipline.
• Chartered Engineer or Incorporated Engineer status with a relevant professional institution, such as IChemE.
• Typically 8–10+ years’ relevant process design experience.
• Background must be from water, wastewater and/or biosolids/sludge treatment design.
• Proven ability to act as process discipline lead or senior technical lead on multidisciplinary projects.
• Strong technical expertise in water/wastewater treatment process design, including process selection, mass balance, process capacity, PFDs, P&IDs and design basis development.
• Practical experience using process modelling/simulation packages such as BioWin, SUMO, Dynamizu or equivalent.
• Strong understanding of UK water industry standards, CDM 2015, process safety, safety-by-design, regulatory drivers and common delivery models.
• Confident client-facing communicator with experience leading workshops, technical reviews and design discussions.
• Experience mentoring or managing engineers and supporting technical capability development.
Desirable Skills / Knowledge
• Deep experience in wastewater treatment, clean water treatment, sludge/bioresources, nutrient removal, water reuse/recycling, process optimisation, chemical dosing, energy recovery or low-carbon design.
• Experience delivering AMP8, WINEP, SRO, D&B, framework, alliance or contractor-led projects.
• Advanced capability in BioWin, SUMO, Dynamizu, process model calibration, scenario testing, dynamic simulation or operational optimisation.
• Experience developing process design standards, calculation tools, modelling workflows, QA processes or reusable digital templates.
• Experience contributing to recruitment, resource planning, bid writing, technical proposals, client presentations or new service development.
Please note that you must have the right to work in the UK to be considered for this position.

• Up to 10% quarterly discretionary bonus
• 25 days holiday (+BH) with the option to buy more
• Private pension
• Private medical insurance
• Paid training, CPD + reimbursed registration fees

• A high performing, supportive clinically led culture
• Clear career routes within Ingeus and the wider APM Group
• Online shopping discounts
• Variety of other financial and lifestyle options
• £2000 refer a friend scheme

About This Job
About the Role
The wind tunnel and CFD tell us what the car should do. The track tells us what it actually does. As our Senior Trackside Aerodynamicist, you are the person who works out the difference. You will be responsible for the aerodynamic performance of the car at the circuit, turning track data into clear aerodynamic understanding and getting it to race engineering fast enough to shape setup decisions while the session is still running.
You will be part of the trackside engineering team and act as the principal link between the Aero Development Race teams. That means owning the quality and interpretation of trackside aero analysis, checking that surfaces, fit, sealing and configuration match specification, and working with the build team to resolve anything that does not. It also means making sure that what we learn at the track goes back into the development programme, so every race weekend makes the next car better. Expect to explain complex aero to engineers and drivers in plain language, often against a ticking clock.
As part of this role, regular travel and race attendance is required.
Key Responsibilities include:
• Owning trackside aerodynamic analysis across all race and test sessions, delivering conclusions within the running schedule
• Interpreting and presenting aero data to engineers and drivers to inform setup decisions and development direction
• Identifying aerodynamic limitations and quantify the lap time cost of each
• Briefing the race team on development items ahead of each event, including the expected gain and how it will be measured
• Improving track-to-tunnel and track-to-CFD correlation, and specify the instrumentation and on-track experiments needed to validate development items
• Developing trackside analysis tools and methodology, and define best practice for the group
• Acting as the point of reference for trackside aerodynamics, working with development aerodynamics, vehicle performance and race engineering to reach agreed conclusions
About You
You are someone who can take a large, noisy dataset and pull out a clear conclusion, then present it clearly and with the right level of confidence. You understand the trade-offs between aerodynamic, mechanical and tyre optima, and you know when a compromise on aero is the right call. You stay calm when the clock is running, and you can make a defensible decision and be honest about the residual risk. You build good relationships easily, whether you are talking to a driver, a race engineer or a designer back at the factory.
What we are looking for:
• A degree in aerodynamics, aeronautical or mechanical engineering, or a closely related discipline (equivalent demonstrable experience is welcome)
• Demonstrable experience in a race car aerodynamics or performance engineering role
• Previous experience in Formula 1 or another elite motorsport category
• Strong working knowledge of full-scale race car data acquisition hardware and software, and their limitations
• Proven data analysis capability in MATLAB, Python or similar, including building and maintaining your own analysis tools
• Willingness and ability to travel internationally throughout the race and test calendar

Additional Information

Atlassian Williams F1 Team is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity and inclusion. We are happy to discuss reasonable job adjustments.

About This Job
The Customer and Accounts platforms are the spine of the Core Banking Platform. The Customer Platform holds the Bank’s single, deduplicated view of every person and organisation we deal with. The Accounts Platform is the layer every system in the Bank goes through to create and service accounts on Thought Machine Vault Core. Every other platform, franchise and squad depends on both.
This role owns the product agenda across the two. You will run a single roadmap, own the API contracts other teams build against, and define how these platforms behave to the level of precision an engineer can build from: how a customer is matched, merged and maintained, how accounts are created and move through their lifecycle, how instructions and events flow to and from Vault Core, and what happens at every boundary and edge case in between.
It is a deliberately deep, hands-on platform role for someone who is energised rather than daunted by data models, API versioning, idempotency and failure modes, and who is comfortable that their users are other engineering teams rather than end customers.
Roadmap & Initiative Definition
• Own a single product roadmap across the Customer and Accounts platforms, sequenced against franchise commercial priorities, Core Banking Programme commitments and the platform’s delivery capacity.
• Balance platform reliability, new capability and migration work in one plan, and make the trade-offs between them explicit rather than letting the loudest demand set the order.
• Run discovery with the squads and franchises that depend on the platform, establishing the underlying customer and business need, the platform behaviour it implies, and whether the platform can support it.
• Convert consumer demand into well-formed initiatives with a clear problem statement, scope, dependencies and definition of success, so the squad has a credible, prioritised pipeline of work.
• Take on the problems that are too large or too cross-cutting for any single product squad to own, the ones that only become solvable when one platform holds the whole picture.
• Own migration and decommissioning planning for legacy customer and account infrastructure, including how records are matched, moved, reconciled and proven correct.
• Bring a point of view. Where a request is poorly formed, unaffordable or better solved elsewhere in the estate, say so early and propose the alternative.
Product Definition on the Platform
• Own how the Customer Platform behaves — matching, merge and deduplication rules, what constitutes the golden record, how customer data is maintained and corrected, and the downstream consequences of any change to that record — including configuration and the rationale behind every parameter choice.
• Own how the Accounts Platform behaves — account creation, lifecycle states and closure, how instructions reach Vault Core, and how posting and event behaviour is exposed back to consuming systems.
• Treat the platform API surface as a product in its own right: own its definition, versioning and documentation, so every consuming system has stable contracts to build against and no consumer is surprised by a change.
• Set the standards for how other squads integrate with the platform, covering integration patterns, idempotency, error handling and testing, and make sure they are understood and followed.
• Translate consumer needs, regulatory obligations and platform constraints into unambiguous requirements, with user stories and acceptance criteria covering happy path, unhappy path, boundary and invalid-input cases.
• Decide whether a need is met by configuration, new platform capability, or a change in the consuming system, and make the trade-off explicit rather than defaulting to build.
• Build in the controls the Bank needs from the outset: FCA and Consumer Duty outcomes, accuracy and lineage of customer and account data, auditable behaviour, and correct treatment under financial crime and data protection obligations.
• Grow the Customer Platform as the Bank’s single source of truth for who we deal with, rather than one more system holding a partial view.
• Make each new product and franchise faster and lower-effort to launch by building reusable capability rather than one-off integrations.
• Review implemented behaviour against requirements alongside engineers, and own product sign-off through test and UAT.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Work day to day with the engineers on the platform squad, not just their leadership, in refinement, in design discussions and in defect triage. The quality of this working relationship is the single biggest determinant of success in the role.
• Partner with the franchise and product squads that consume the platform, and hold the line on platform integrity under delivery pressure, balancing franchise urgency against consistent, scalable foundations.
• Work with Operations to understand how customers and accounts are actually onboarded and serviced, and bring that reality into platform decisions.
• Engage Finance, Data, Legal and Risk & Compliance early, so reporting needs, regulatory change and control expectations shape requirements rather than arriving as late constraints.
• Communicate platform and integration decisions in plain language to non-technical stakeholders, and in exacting detail to engineers. Both audiences should recognise the same decision.
• Use data to understand platform performance, and present roadmap and strategy to senior leadership, including the quarterly Technology Platform Playback attended by the CTO.
Interfaces & Boundaries
• The Product Lead, Core Banking Platform owns cross-book demand consolidation, investment business cases and prioritisation. This role supplies the platform substance those business cases rest on.
• The Vault Platform Product Manager owns the Vault implementation across the Bank and all product lines on it. This role owns the customer and account layer in front of it, and the two agree the seam between platform behaviour and product behaviour rather than each assuming it.
• Product Managers for each lending product line own their own product definition on Vault Core. This role owns the shared customer and account capability underneath them, and escalates cross-product-line trade-offs rather than resolving them locally.
• The Core Banking Delivery Lead and Engineering Manager own delivery sequencing and capacity. This role owns what is being built and why, and whether what was built is right.
• Data owns the Bank’s data architecture and governance. This role owns the customer record as a product and works within that architecture.

About This Job
Important Eligibility Criteria
To be eligible for this fully remote role, you must live outside of London, Essex, and the South East of England.
If you currently live within these areas, please visit our website to explore our Hybrid Functional Assessor opportunities, which may be more suitable.
• Starting Salary £42,985
• Fully remote role
• Full time Monday - Friday 9.00am - 5.00pm
• Further salary uplifts as you learn new specialist skills from year 2.
• Up to 10% quarterly discretionary bonus
• 25 days holiday (+BH) with the option to buy more
Are you looking to your clinical skills in a different way? As a Functional Assessor, you'll continue to utilise your clinical expertise, maintain your registration, and enjoy a better work-life balance. If you have a minimum of 12 months' post-registration experience and have been practising as a clinician throughout the last year, we'd love to hear from you. If you are a pharmacist, we welcome your application if you have a minimum of 18 months experience.
What you’ll be doing as a Functional Assessor:
• Liaising directly with claimants, using active listening and questioning skills to obtain additional evidence where needed in order to complete the assessment.
• Liaising with clinical peers across the NHS and private healthcare sector, charities, and support organisations to obtain and evaluate evidence that assists in the production of detailed assessment reports.
• Triaging cases to determine the assessment route a case will take.
• Conducting initial case reviews, file work and paper-based assessments.
• Applying critical thinking and logical reasoning to produce accurate and detailed reports on each case.
As a Functional Assessor with Ingeus you can expect:
• Predictable hours
• Up to 10% quarterly discretionary bonus
• 25 days holiday (+BH) with the option to buy more
• Private pension
• Private medical insurance
• Maternity and Parental Leave
• Paid training, CPD + reimbursed registration fees
• Paid, structured training to achieve formal DWP accreditation
• A high performing, supportive clinically led culture
• Clear career routes within Ingeus and the wider APM Group
• Online shopping discounts
• Variety of other financial and lifestyle options
• £2000 refer a friend scheme
Is this role right for you?
Many clinicians find the role of a Functional Assessor rewarding, but it’s also challenging at the same time and it’s not the right fit for everyone.
This role would suit someone who:
• Thrives on service excellence in a high performing working environment that offers structure and the opportunity to use your clinical skills in a different way.
• Is open to a formalised programme of training to become a DWP approved Functional Assessor.
• Is receptive to ongoing constructive feedback, ensuring our claimants continually get the very best experience.
• Has confidence in their ability to use computers and in learning different software packages to complete detailed, high-quality reports for all claimants assessed.
This role may not be the best match for you if:
• You are not comfortable using or are unfamiliar with technology.
• You dislike writing detailed reports.
• You prefer a more hands on approach to clinical care.
• You’re not looking for a new direction nor a period of retraining into a new role.
• You don’t enjoy working in an environment with targets.
• You are not looking for a role that requires you to work on site for some or all of your working week.3 days a week.
We look forward to receiving your application!

Qualifications
Who We’re Looking For
• NMC-registered Adult Nurses (RGN, RMN, RNLD) or HCPC-registered Physiotherapists, Occupational Therapists and Paramedics or GPHC-registered Pharmacists.
With excellent communication & critical-thinking skills, the ability to type and confidence using computers

If you require any support or adjustments—whether that’s help with the application, interview format, or anything else—we’re here to listen and work with you to find the best approach. About This Job
Principal Structural Engineer
London
We invite you to bring your talent and passion into play as you take an active role in delivering a wide range of interesting projects of different scales, complexities, structural forms and materials within a Top 10 consultancy. If you crave a challenging role but need flexibility and work-life balance, our new Senior/Principal Structural Engineer position may be ideal for you. We are very interested in talking to people who are looking for a new challenge or may be on a career break and are thinking about returning to consultancy.
Are you our new Principal Structural Engineer? Click the “I’m interested” button to send your application.
Inviting bright minds
Do you want to push the boundaries of your profession and develop your excellence in an open, collaborative and empowering culture? We work to create a sustainable future and our inspiring projects and innovative solutions aim to set the standard among our peers. You will join a foundation-owned global company that has been growing successfully since its founding in 1945. Together, we lead and leave a positive impact on societies, companies and people around the world.
You will join our Industry and Infrastructure Facilities team in London
As our new Principal Structural Engineer, you will be part of our Industry and Infrastructure Facilities team in our London office working on a range of exciting local landmarks as well as national and international projects. This team delivers projects across sectors such as Rail, Aviation, Data Centres and other critical facilities, combining sector-specific technical expertise with Ramboll’s broader multidisciplinary capabilities. We have won many awards for our work, regularly support research and have a very collaborative culture. We operate a fun and inquisitive office environment and actively encourage design flair and innovative solutions.
Your key tasks and responsibilities will involve:
• Develop and agree structural concepts and design philosophies
• Inspire and enthuse the engineers and technicians on your projects
• Liaise with clients and collaborators, representing Ramboll at project meetings
• Take ownership as day-to-day lead on a project or part of a project
• Push the boundaries of low-carbon design
Your key deliverables over the first 12 months will be:
• Grow and maintain a network of contacts and be a great ambassador for Ramboll
• Lead the design process for a project (size suitable for level of experience)
• Outside day-to-day project work, collaborate with colleagues from the London team and beyond to support implementation of various aspects of the Ramboll Business Plan
Your starting point for constant growth
From the moment you join Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional development so that you grow with the company. We provide growth and development opportunities in a supportive environment with flexible and hybrid working, and care about our people’s wellbeing.
For this role, we believe your starting point is:
• Chartered with the IStructE, ICE, or international equivalent
• An excellent communicator capable of explaining complex engineering principles in plain language, verbally, in writing, and through sketching
• Demonstrable experience in at least one of the following infrastructure sectors: Rail, Aviation, Data Centres (or other critical facilities); experience across multiple sectors is highly desirable
• A track record of working on projects with high levels of design, sustainability, or re-use of existing assets
• Experience in the design of primary construction materials (steel, concrete, timber) and a good general knowledge of building construction; experience of MMC would be beneficial.
• A passion for sustainable solutions
• A multidisciplinary mindset and an aptitude for learning about the wider aspects of building design
Personal qualities that will help you succeed in this role include:
• Great with people
• Diverse in outlook and with something different to bring to the table
• A curiosity to explore – ‘is there a better way to do this’
• Happy to ask questions and to answer them!
• Willingness to take responsibility for your projects and development
Essential requirements:
We are also interested in any experience you may have in the following areas, but these are not essential:
• Assessment, retrofit and alteration of existing structures
• Construction supervision, building investigation and structural testing
Welcome to our Buildings division
As one of the top 10 building designers in the world, Ramboll works on more than 10,000 building projects each year. 5,000 experts across the world specialise in creating more innovative, sustainable and liveable buildings. We place particular emphasis on our liveable buildings concept where we balance the cultural, social and physical values of buildings, to improve the quality of life for building users.
Ramboll in the United Kingdom
Ramboll is ranked a Top 10 consultant in the UK and has 1,300 bright minds working across 17 offices to apply their passion to deliver innovative solutions across society. We love seeing our talents develop and succeed and you will have opportunities to work on challenging and inspiring projects within an environment that is friendly, open and supportive.
Ramboll offers the opportunity to be part of a dynamic organisation in the rapidly growing Engineering and Consultancy sector in the UK. We offer a competitive salary, alongside 27 days holiday per year, private medical insurance and flexible working.
How to apply
Apply online. Attach your CV, cover letter and relevant documents showcasing why you are the right fit for the role, and when you are available to start. We look forward to receiving your application.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/asos/7440001540.description_excerpt:
About This Job
About The Role
ASOS is looking for a Brand Planning Manager to join the Brand & Planning Marketing team. This is a planning role responsible for leading, translating brand and business strategy into one integrated, prioritised and executable global brand plan.
The role sits at the handover point between strategy and execution. It will connect Brand Strategy, Brand Marketing, Brand Heat, Product, Commercial, Performance Marketing, Creative, channel teams, agencies and local markets, turning strategic direction into clear annual and seasonal plans, market-ready calendars, channel roles, investment principles and measurable outcomes.
Working closely with the Global Brand & Planning Marketing Lead, the Brand Planning Manager will own the day-to-day planning rhythm across the year, lead market engagement and the communications model, and create the clarity, governance and decision points needed to move plans forward. The role will not own campaign creative briefing. Its focus is ensuring that strategy is translated into an aligned plan which enables teams to brief, develop and execute effectively.
This role will combine integrated planning leadership, market partnership, cross-functional influence and operational ownership, while providing senior direction and quality assurance across the team’s reporting and effectiveness work so that insight consistently feeds forward into future plans.
Why This Role Matters
The Brand & Planning Marketing team is building a more connected operating system across planning, execution and effectiveness. The Brand Planning Manager will help create the capacity and senior ownership needed for the Global Brand & Planning Marketing Lead to focus primarily on strategic planning, while ensuring reporting remains well governed, decision-oriented and connected to the plan.
The role will act as a planning control tower for Brand Marketing: creating one view of the global and local calendar, clarifying ownership and dependencies, bringing market “Fit to Win” needs into planning, and ensuring agreed plans move confidently from strategic direction into channel and market execution.
What You Will Be Responsible For
1. Integrated Annual & Seasonal Brand Planning
• Maintain the integrated full-year brand plan and four seasonal plans, connecting brand priorities, product and commercial inputs, customer and cultural moments, campaign types, channel roles, markets and investment.
• Translate strategy into clear planning parameters, priorities, phasing, sequencing, success measures and decision points that enable execution teams to develop channel and campaign responses.
• Lead the day-to-day annual and seasonal planning rhythm, including planning forums, inputs, working sessions, readiness reviews, decision logs and senior stakeholder updates.
• Ensure the plan balances long-term brand building with traffic and commercial priorities, with clear roles across Brand Marketing, Volume Collaborations, Brand Heat and Performance Marketing.
• Maintain a single source of truth across planning documents, calendars, milestones, assumptions, ownership and dependencies, surfacing gaps, overlaps and risks early.
• Use performance evidence, customer insight, product priorities, market context and previous learnings to improve future plans and recommendations.
2. Market Planning, Calendars & “Fit to Win”
• Act as the day-to-day Brand Planning point of contact for local market marketing teams, building a consistent two-way planning rhythm between central and local teams.
• Own the global market marketing calendar, bringing together global campaigns, locally relevant moments, product availability, adaptable assets, media support, market-led activations and key dependencies.
• Lead the process to understand each priority market’s “Fit to Win”: the customer, commercial, cultural, media and executional needs required for activity to succeed locally.
• Ensure market needs are considered early enough to shape the central plan, rather than being managed only at handover, while maintaining clear global priorities and guardrails.
• Drive bilateral alignment on where markets will amplify global activity, where localisation is required, where locally led activity is more appropriate, and what support, ownership and funding are needed.
• Create clear market handovers and participation views, escalating unresolved trade-offs and ensuring final decisions are reflected in one integrated global plan.
3. Communications Model & Channel Integration
• Drive the ASOS communications model, translating brand objectives and audience priorities into clear roles for paid, owned and earned channels across campaigns and always-on activity.
• Partner with Brand Strategy, Consumer Insight, Performance Marketing, Media, Social, PR, Talent, CRM, Homepage/App, Search and other channel teams to define how channels work together across the customer journey.
• Establish practical planning principles for channel role, audience, message, format, timing, sequencing, weighting and investment, ensuring these are applied consistently in annual and seasonal plans.
• Use effectiveness evidence and channel learnings to evolve the communications model, resolve duplication or gaps, and strengthen the connection between reach, consideration, traffic and commercial outcomes.
• Drive adoption of the model through clear tools, playbooks, forums and governance, ensuring it becomes a working planning framework rather than a standalone strategy document.
4. Strategy-to-Execution Handover & GTM Governance
• Own the planning handover from strategic direction into executable GTM plans, making sure teams understand the objective, role of the moment, audience, market implications, channel parameters, investment guardrails and measures of success.
• Partner with Brand Project Management and execution leads to translate the integrated plan into workstreams, critical paths, owners, milestones and dependencies without taking ownership of campaign creative briefing.
• Create clear governance across planning and execution, including who decides, who contributes, when decisions are required and how changes to scope, timing or investment are managed.
• Monitor readiness against the agreed plan, identify misalignment or delivery risk early, facilitate resolution and escalate material decisions to the Global Brand Planning Lead.
• Connect Brand, Product, Commercial, Creative, Media, channels, agencies and markets around one plan, reducing duplicated planning and fragmented handovers.
• Codify and continuously improve the Brand Planning playbook, including planning processes, roles, rituals, templates, decision rights and best practice.
5. Effectiveness, Reporting Oversight & Feed-Forward
• Ensure the reporting and effectiveness agenda is anchored to the priorities, KPIs and decisions set through the annual and seasonal planning process.
• Support with senior direction and quality assurance across weekly performance reporting,

About This Job
This role is for a builder who loves coaching.
Early this year, Sportradar launched its first Sales Development function. The team now generates pipeline across more than ten product lines in four regions, partners closely with Account Executives and owns its own pipeline. The foundations and the culture are set. What comes next is making the motion consistent, measurable and scalable.
You will be the first dedicated manager of this team, reporting to the Senior Director of Sales Development and Enablement. Your focus is people: getting the absolute best from every SDR, building the standards they operate to, and shaping how Sales Development evolves as the business grows.
We want someone who has built a founding SDR team before, knows what great looks like in B2B SaaS, and is excited to rip up what isn't working and try again, in a business at the forefront of sport.
THE CHALLENGE
• Coaching and performance: Run a consistent coaching cadence across every region: 1:1s, call and email reviews, sequence feedback and skill development plans. Raise the bar on quality, not just volume.
• Playbooks and standardisation: Revamp the SDR playbook (still a work in progress!) and create shared standards across regions, while leaving room for what works locally. Make “how we prospect” something every SDR can explain and repeat.
• Metrics and accountability: Own team performance against meetings held, SQOs, pipeline generated and outbound activity. Define and enforce the activity standards that drive them, including calling discipline.
• Onboarding and ramp: Build a structured ramp path that gets new SDRs productive faster, and prove it with data.
• SDR to AE partnership: Strengthen the handoff so every meeting lands with the right context. Build trust with sales leaders and turn sceptics into advocates.
• Competitive and market readiness: Partner with Enablement and Product Marketing to upskill SDRs in competitive and product knowledge across the portfolio.
• AI and future-proofing: Lead how the team uses AI to research, personalise and prioritise. Encourage creativity and experimentation so the SDR role evolves with AI.
• Operating rhythm: Design team cadences, competitions and rituals that keep energy and focus high across time zones.
• Hiring and development: Partner on hiring and build clear progression paths so top SDRs grow with Sportradar.
ABOUT YOU:
• Experience building or scaling a founding SDR team in a B2B SaaS scale-up
• A track record managing SDRs across multiple regions and time zones
• Background in sport, media, advertising technology or data
• Power-user fluency in Outreach and Salesforce
• A coach-first style. You develop people in the room, not only from a dashboard
• A collaborative instinct. You partner with sales leadership, Enablement, RevOps and Marketing
• A clear view on how AI will reshape the Sales Development role, and how to prepare a team for it
• Comfort with ambiguity and a habit of documenting as you build
• A bias for quality over activity, and ownership of outcomes, not tasks
• APAC or LATAM market experience
• Previous experience with Product Manager and Marketing personas
• Experience partnering with Enablement on certification or ramp programmes
OUR OFFER
• A collaborative environment with colleagues from all over the world (Engineering offices in Europe, Asia and US) including various social events and teambuilding.
• Flexibility to manage your workday and tasks with autonomy.
• A balance of structure and autonomy to tackle your daily tasks.
• Vibrant and inclusive community, including Women in Tech and Pride groups which welcome all participants.
• Global Employee Assistance Programme.
• Calm and Reulay app (leading well-being apps designed to support focus, quality rest, mindfulness, and long-term mental resilience).
• Online training videos.
• ​​​​​​​Flexible working hours.
While we appreciate the flexibility and benefits of working from home, we strongly believe that coming together in person fosters stronger connections, encourages collaboration, and drives innovation—both as individuals and as a company. The energy, shared ideas, and team support we experience in the office strengthen the foundation of our success and culture. For this reason, we are an office-first business operating a on-site model, with team members working in the office four days a week to build relationships, exchange ideas, and grow together.
OUR RECRUITMENT PROCESS
• Initial Screening: A quick chat with our Talent Acquisition Partner to understand your background and expectations.
• Video Interview: Meet with the Hiring Manager to dive into the role and also discuss team fit.
• Onsite Interview: Meet with the local team and take a tour of our office for a final meet-and-greet.

Our Ground Engineering team in the United Kingdom and Ireland (UK&I) comprises 150 professionals who provide a comprehensive range of services, including project management, feasibility studies, ground investigation design and interpretation, detailed design, contract administration, and construction supervision. We work on ground engineering projects across the UK&I and internationally, supporting both internal and external clients. Our primary focus areas include energy, water, nuclear (decommissioning and new build), power, road and rail, aviation, ports and harbours, as well as commercial and industrial developments, and landslip investigation and remediation.
We work for leading UK and International clients, including National Grid, BP, Sellafield, Associated British Ports, Transport Scotland, National Highways, Transport Infrastructure Ireland, Network Rail, and local authorities, as well as for prominent contractors and developers. Our impressive portfolio features a range of regional and national projects, such as the Great Grid Upgrade, STEP Fusion,  pumped storage hydro projects in the Scottish Highlands, Snowdonia VIP, A83 Rest and be Thankful, M54-M6 Link Road, water schemes for various water utilities clients (UK&I) and HMNB Devonport redevelopment. Additionally, we are involved in overseas projects such as Eastlink in Sweden.
As a Ground Engineering Apprentice, you will work alongside experienced geotechnical engineers and engineering geologists whilst studying towards a Level 6 Degree Apprenticeship in either Civil Engineering or Geoscience. You will gain practical experience across a variety of ground engineering projects, developing the technical knowledge necessary to build a successful career within the industry.

About This Job
Principal Product Manager, 12 Month Fixed Term Contract (FTC)
Job Description
At Genomics England, we’re looking for an experienced Principal Product Manager to provide product leadership for work on the trustworthy stewardship of genomic data and how we manage our relationship with those who choose to share their data for research.
Our products and services operate in a uniquely sensitive environment. They must enable genomic data to be used responsibly for research while respecting the choices, expectations and trust of the people whose data makes this work possible.
This creates complex product challenges that extend beyond a single feature, journey or team. They involve multiple products, people, policies, data, and technologies. They span operations and governance, with decisions that have lasting implications for participants, researchers, healthcare services and Genomics England.
This is where you will make a difference
As a proven Principal Product Manager, you’ll lead a strategically important product area that is an organisational priority. You will partner with the programme lead to set its vision, strategy and intended outcomes while coordinating discovery, direction and delivery across related products, services and squads. You will support with the leadership of the wider team, deputising for the programme lead where required.
You’ll establish clarity where the path is uncertain, bring teams and senior stakeholders together around shared outcomes, and translate strategic direction into meaningful OKRs, coherent roadmaps and focused priorities.
You’ll initially lead the team through early discovery product work, with a view to shaping delivery further down the line. This means ensuring we understand the right problems and gathering requirements before committing to solutions, using evidence to test assumptions and helping cross functional teams create products and services that are useful, feasible, responsible and sustainable.
This is a Principal individual contributor role with meaningful scope to influence beyond a single squad. You’ll connect related work, manage complex dependencies and help teams make effective product decisions while remaining close enough to delivery to understand where support, challenge or intervention is needed.
You’ll collaborate with participants, user researchers, designers, architects, engineers, data specialists, policy and governance colleagues, operational teams and senior leaders. Through clear direction, constructive challenge and inclusive decision making, you’ll help people navigate competing priorities and make thoughtful trade-offs.
You’ll also play a leadership role within the wider product management chapter at Genomics England, owning cross-chapter initiatives, mentoring Product Managers and helping to drive excellent practice across teams. You may have direct line management responsibility for 1-2 product people.
Why this role matters
Participants are central to genomic research. Maintaining their trust requires more than meeting regulatory obligations. It means understanding their needs and expectations, involving them meaningfully and designing products and services that handle their choices and data responsibly.
As Principal Product Manager, you’ll help shape how Genomics England approaches these challenges, with consideration to the full product lifecycle, creating a clear connection between participant needs, organisational priorities and the work of multidisciplinary teams.
Your impact will be seen in the product direction you establish, the difficult decisions you support the Programme Lead to navigate and the products and services that emerge from that work, ultimately helping Genomics England maintain trusted relationships with participants and enable the responsible use of genomic data for research.
What you’ll be doing
•

About This Job
Join us in preserving engineering heritage while pioneering the future of resilient water infrastructure! You will help to deliver industry-leading reservoir and dam projects across the UK and further afield, including safety upgrades, hydropower, new storage and resilience schemes.
Our graduates gain valuable experience working on a variety of projects alongside a multitude of different disciplines. Our graduates are encouraged to develop their understanding of many elements within the water industry, such as hydraulic, structural, geotechnical and environmental design through calculations, report writing and use of engineering software. You will work alongside our experienced engineers and consultants as you develop these skills within a positive culture where learning and development is actively supported and promoted.

• Undertake numerical analysis including the use of specialist software to assist with the study of dams and reservoirs

• Undertake feasibility studies to appraise the practicability of alternative solutions, including considerations such as technical performance, health and safety, cost, environmental benefits
• Prepare designs, drawings, specifications and contracts
• Write clear, concise reports and prepare presentations for colleagues, clients and regulators
• Join site visits to support dam inspections and broaden your understanding of how assets perform in the real world.
Examples of projects we’re working on:
• Exploring potential locations for new reservoirs across the Southwest—helping clients plan long-term resilience in the face of climate change.
• Designing eight dams as part of the Loch Kemp pumped storage hydro scheme—supporting the energy transition with large-scale, flexible low-carbon infrastructure.
• Upgrading ageing dams to maintain safety and performance, including historic lakes with significant heritage value—balancing safety, sustainability, and cultural importance.
• Helping clients across the UK maintain safe dams and compliance with the Reservoirs Act 1975, including carrying out statutory inspections, designing upgrades and planning for emergencies.
• Supporting our colleagues in the USA with the risk assessment of a portfolio of dams, helping to understand the key areas where works can deliver improvements in dam safety.

• A bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Water Resources Engineering, or a related field (e.g. geology, geotechnics, structures).

• Water-related modules or relevant work experience would be an advantage.
• Enthusiastic, hard-working and technically proficient.
• Curiosity and an inquisitive mindset, with strong research skills.
• Interest in reservoir engineering and the wider water industry.
• Good written and verbal communication skills, considering technical stakeholders, clients and members of the public.
• Structure & prioritise work effectively through close cooperation with multi-disciplinary teams.

Capability to consider client and business expectations and be able to consider the wider financial and commercial implications of your actions.

About This Job
For Universal United Kingdom Resort (UUKR), the Site Planning Compliance Manager is a fully site-based role (5 days a week) embedded within the live construction environment, responsible for overseeing contractor activities and ensuring planning requirements are understood, implemented, and maintained across the Entertainment Resort Complex (ERC).
Working closely with contractors, site managers and delivery teams on a day-to-day basis, the Site Planning Compliance Manager acts as the key on-site interface for planning compliance. The role provides practical oversight of construction activities, undertaking regular site inspections, identifying potential or actual areas of non-compliance, and working directly with contractors to agree and implement corrective actions. A key focus is translating planning permissions, conditions and statutory obligations into clear, workable requirements that can be effectively applied within an active and complex construction program.
The role is responsible for monitoring contractor compliance with requirements including Construction Environmental Management Plans (CEMPs), habitat protection and enhancement measures, flood mitigation conditions, working hour restrictions, approved methodologies, and all applicable Special Development Order (SDO) conditions. The Site Planning Compliance Manager works proactively with contractors, consultants and internal teams to ensure these obligations are consistently embedded within site operations.
Alongside day-to-day contractor management and site oversight, the role supports the preparation, review and coordination of planning compliance documentation, bringing practical construction insight to contractor submissions and proposed methodologies. The Site Planning Compliance Manager also plays a key role in preparing for and facilitating site visits by governmental, planning and regulatory bodies, ensuring the site is ready and that compliance requirements can be clearly demonstrated.
Through regular engagement with contractors and site teams, the Site Planning Compliance Manager will foster a strong culture of planning compliance, ensuring obligations are clearly communicated, understood and consistently implemented throughout all phases of construction.
MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES
• Act as the primary on-site representative for planning compliance, working closely with contractors, site managers, and subcontractors to ensure clear understanding and consistent application of planning requirements within day-to-day construction activities.
• Monitor and enforce site-wide compliance with planning permissions, planning conditions, and approved documentation including CEMPs, method statements, environmental management plans, and SDO requirements. Undertake daily site inspections to verify that all contractor activities align with approved submissions.
• Identify, manage, and resolve non-compliance issues, working collaboratively with contractors to implement corrective actions. Provide practical, construction-informed guidance to support compliance, including development of revised methodologies, mitigation measures, and improved site practices.
• Support the development and submission of planning documentation, including reviewing contractor submissions, contributing construction-based insight, and ensuring proposed approaches are realistic, compliant, and deliverable on site.
• Lead engagement and coordination for external stakeholder interactions, including site visits from governmental bodies (e.g. MHCLG), planning authorities, and regulatory stakeholders.
• Ensure site readiness and accurate representation of compliance status.
• Drive awareness and education of planning requirements across the workforce, including participation in workshops, toolbox talks, and site briefings. Develop and share practical tools, guidance, and communications to embed compliance within site culture
• Understand and actively participate in Environmental, Health & Safety responsibilities by following established Universal policy, procedures, training and team member involvement activities.

Qualifications
• Willing to be onsite 5 days a week in Bedford.
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification in Construction Management, Environmental Management, Planning, Engineering, or a related field is preferred.
• Significant experience in construction site-based roles with strong understanding of live construction environments and contractor operations.
• Proven experience in planning compliance, planning conditions, or environmental management within major construction or infrastructure projects.
• Strong working knowledge of planning permissions, CEMPs, environmental constraints, and regulatory compliance requirements.
• Ability to interpret planning and environmental requirements and translate them into practical, buildable site solutions.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage effectively at all levels from site operatives to senior stakeholders.
• Strong observational and problem-solving skills with a proactive, solution-oriented mindset.
• Experience delivering or contributing to site training, workshops, or toolbox talks is desirable.
• Microsoft (MS) Excel, Word, Planner, Power BI, Teams, Power Apps.
• Experience with document management systems and PDF tools (e.g., Bluebeam) preferred.
• Experience with Wrike or similar tools is a plus.

About This Job
We are looking for an experienced Senior Service Designer to work within a multidisciplinary team delivering complex digital services for a UK public sector client.
You will lead service design activity across the service lifecycle, working from Discovery and Alpha through Beta and Live, depending on the assignment. You will help teams understand complex service landscapes, identify user and organisational needs, and design coherent end-to-end services across digital and non-digital channels.
Working alongside user researchers, interaction designers, content designers, product managers, business analysts, delivery managers, developers, architects, policy colleagues and operational teams, you will ensure services are designed around user needs while considering policy, technology and operational constraints.
You will be expected to work confidently within a GOV.UK Service Standard and Government Digital and Data environment, helping teams make evidence-based design decisions and prepare services for assessment where required.
Key responsibilities
You will:
• Lead service design activity within an Agile multidisciplinary delivery team.
• Map as-is and to-be services, identifying pain points, dependencies, opportunities and gaps across the end-to-end journey.
• Create and maintain service blueprints, journey maps, service maps, ecosystem maps and other appropriate service-design artefacts.
• Understand the relationship between user-facing journeys and the processes, people, policy, data and technology that support them.
• Translate user research, analytics, operational insight and wider evidence into actionable service improvements.
• Work closely with user researchers to ensure service decisions are grounded in a strong understanding of user needs.
• Collaborate with interaction and content designers to create coherent experiences across digital and non-digital touchpoints.
• Work with product, business analysis, architecture, technology, policy and operational colleagues to understand constraints and design viable services.
• Plan and facilitate workshops, co-design sessions, service-mapping activities and collaborative decision-making.
• Prototype service concepts and test assumptions early, iterating designs based on evidence and feedback.
• Identify dependencies and systemic issues that may affect the successful delivery of the service.
• Communicate complex service journeys and design decisions clearly to senior stakeholders and multidisciplinary teams.
• Build consensus around service-design approaches while constructively challenging assumptions where necessary.
• Contribute to Service Standard assessments and assurance activity where required.
• Champion accessibility, inclusion and user-centred design throughout delivery.

Qualifications
We are particularly interested in contractors who can demonstrate:
• Strong experience as a Senior Service Designer within UK central government, wider public sector or another GDS-aligned environment.
• Practical experience designing services in line with the GOV.UK Service Standard and user-centred design principles.
• Experience working across one or more government delivery phases such as Discovery, Alpha, Beta or Live.
• Evidence of designing complex services end-to-end, and across multiple channels.
• Strong service mapping and visualisation skills, including service blueprints, user journeys and ecosystem/service maps.
• Experience translating user research and other evidence into service-design decisions.
• Strong workshop facilitation and co-design skills.
• Experience working with a broad range of stakeholders, including senior stakeholders, policy, operational and technical colleagues.
• Ability to navigate ambiguity, bring structure to complex problems and establish a clear service-design direction.
• Strong understanding of accessibility and inclusive design, including designing for users with different access needs.
• Ability to communicate and defend design decisions using clear evidence.
• Experience identifying measures or success criteria that can be used to understand service performance and impact.
• Experience using collaborative design and mapping tools such as Miro, Lucid or equivalent, with an understanding of Figma or similar prototyping tools.
• Experience preparing for or contributing to GOV.UK Service Standard assessments.
• Experience working on services involving complex policy, operational, data or technology dependencies.

We have an exciting opportunity for a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer to join our Powertrain Hydraulics group, contributing to a wide range of assemblies throughout the F1 car with a particular focus on hydraulic, pneumatic, and gearbox systems.
Collaborating with the Group Principal and Head of Powertrain, you will be responsible for the design and integration of hydraulic and pneumatic components that interface with the power unit and transmission systems. You will take ownership of projects from concept through to prototype, testing, and race deployment, working closely with other engineering departments to ensure world-class performance and reliability.
About You
With a deep understanding of hydraulic and pneumatic system design, you bring hands-on expertise in gearbox or powertrain hydraulic systems, confidently selecting pumps, valves, actuators, accumulators, and other critical components, and packaging them efficiently within tight spatial constraints.
Your strong grasp of engineering fundamentals - materials, stress, and fluid mechanics - underpins every decision you make, and your background includes a relevant engineering degree (Mechanical, Automotive, or Aerospace), supported by practical design experience in motorsport, aerospace, or precision engineering. You’re fluent in CAD and ideally familiar with Siemens NX, but you’re just as capable of adapting quickly if your experience lies with other platforms.

• Leading the concept, design, and detailing of mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic components and assemblies across the powertrain and chassis.
• Designing and integrating gearbox hydraulic systems, including actuation, lubrication, and control circuits.
• Performing stress, flow, and sizing calculations to support component and system design decisions, with clear supporting documentation.
• Conducting design reviews independently or alongside the Principal Engineer and Head of Department.
• Deputising for the Principal Engineer and Head of Department when required.

This is a rare opportunity to shape a core technology platform that will be deployed across multiple next-generation military aircraft programmes. You'll influence the architecture of advanced mission systems used on fast jets, helicopters and UAVs for years to come.

• Own the Verification & Validation (V&V) cycle, ensuring testing is comprehensively planned and delivered to achieve full sign-off of product design, with complete traceability to requirements models maintained throughout the development lifecycle
• Collaborate with mechanical, hardware, firmware, and software engineering teams to ensure seamless integration and system compatibility across all project deliverables, promoting adoption of MBSE practices across disciplines
• Lead technical design reviews and provide expert guidance to junior engineers on both traditional systems engineering and model-based systems engineering methodologies, fostering knowledge sharing and continuous improvement - Develop and maintain detailed technical documentation, including design specifications, architecture diagrams, and SysMLv2 models, ensuring alignment between document-based and model-based representations
• Ensure all Digital IO card designs comply with relevant industry standards, regulatory requirements, and organisational quality standards for defence applications - Analyse emerging technologies and industry trends to inform future Digital IO card development strategies and systems engineering practices

Qualifications
Required Skills & Experience
• Proven experience in systems engineering with a focus on processor or hardware design
• Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with meticulous attention to detail
• Knowledge of FPGA architectures and system-level design principles
• Excellent technical documentation and communication skills
• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary engineering teams
Desirable Skills & Experience

• Experience with hardware validation, testing methodologies, and performance analysis

• Knowledge of industry standards such as PCIe, DDR, and other relevant specifications
• Experience with power management, thermal analysis, and signal integrity considerations
• Background in systems architecture and platform-level design
• Understanding of design for manufacturability (DFM) and cost optimisation principles
• Experience working with or familiarity with AI/ML models is preferred

Catch22 provides young people aged 4 to 18 with alternative and special education in order for them to progress and succeed in sustained education or employment. We do this through high quality teaching and learning based on effective relationships that enable the achievement of life skills and meaningful qualifications.

As Key Worker at Include Norfolk you will manage, support and develop a group of young people and their families. You’ll oversee a holistic person-centred approach to a young person’s journey from entry to exit, bridging the gap between their academic, behavioural and therapeutic needs, whilst simultaneously preparing them for post-16.
The Key Worker will develop individual pupil support plans that brings together internal, external and multi-agency professionals in order to support development, attainment and progression.

• To track pastoral progress of the young people in your caseload with regards to school attainment, classroom behaviour and risk of exclusion in order to inform development and review of intervention content.
• Under the guidance of the Pastoral Site Lead or Assistant Headteacher liaise with, and make referrals to, other agencies where necessary.

• To ensure all behaviours within school are managed effectively and timely inline with the behaviour policy.
For Resources
• Keep accurate records, which might be used in case conferences and regular professional meetings.
• To efficiently record all details of each contact or work session with young people using the agreed database system, to keep that data management system up to date and to produce reports to support case reviews and evaluations as requested.
• Ensure the effective and efficient management and organisation of learning and patoral resources, including digital technologies.
